## Reflection

Mid-dose acquisitions correctly moved the call off the early high-dose mislead: 1 uM cell_area z=+9.6 with nuc_area z=+6.0 and 10 uM cell_area z=+10.5 with cell_count z=-7.0, plus atlas e9 with DNA replication 7/10 and DNA damage 2/10 and e13 tied at DNA replication 4/10 and DNA damage 4/10, narrowed the mechanism to the DNA axis and correctly deprioritized microtubule stabilizers and protein degradation/synthesis from the pooled e6 comparison.

- Recovered from early microtubule stabilizer call from e4 and pooled protein degradation/synthesis call from e6 by using dose-separated atlas e9 and e13 that pointed to DNA axis
- Recognized high-dose 30 uM phenotype with cell_count z=-11.6 and nuc_form_factor z=-11.9 as largely cytotoxicity secondary to specific 1-10 uM enlarged cell/nucleus phenotype with cell_area z=+9.6 to +10.5
- Retained DNA damage as second hypothesis at 0.19-0.20 and noted microscopist DNA damage candidate in e5 rather than dismissing it entirely

What was wrong or missed:
- Selected DNA replication over DNA damage despite e13 being a 4/10 versus 4/10 tie and e9 retaining DNA damage 2/10, overweighting replication label
- Interpreted cell_area and nuc_area enlargement at 1, 3 and 10 uM as replication-specific without gamma-H2AX, comet, or EdU evidence that would separate crosslink damage from primary replication blockade
- Exhausted well budget before reviewer-requested c4 replicate phenotyping and substituted weak dose_response trends with n=4 and p up to 0.6 instead of acquiring the requested breadth check

Proposed next experiment: Co-stain for gamma-H2AX foci plus cisplatin-DNA adducts with EdU pulse and DNA-content flow cytometry to test DNA crosslink damage with S/G2 arrest versus primary replication inhibition.
